scenes.headline: How sparse attention picks what to read
scenes.sub: A cheap indexer scores every token; the real attention reads the top 2,048
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pemberton! Most open models without full attention now work this way. Here's how.

scenes.title: Two ways to decode one token

left.title: Dense attention
left.say: Dense attention reads every cached token, for every new one.

right.title: Index-selected
right.say: Index-selected attention scores them all cheaply, then reads only the best two thousand and forty-eight.

steps.term: Indexer: a small scorer in front of attention
steps.say: The new token goes to the indexer, a second, much smaller attention.
It scores every cached token with a ReLU, and keeps the top scores.
Those positions point into the cache, which still holds everything.
The main attention gathers just those entries and runs a normal softmax over them.

scenes.title: The index score
scenes.say: The score for one past token is a weighted sum over a few indexer heads.

parts.note: each head's small query against one shared index key
parts.say: Each head dots its own small query with that token's index key.
A ReLU replaces the softmax. The paper chose it for speed.

parts.note: a weight per head, from the query token
parts.say: And a weight per head, also from the query, mixes them.

steps.say: In DeepSeek's figure, the indexer is the green path. It feeds a top-k selector in front of the core attention.

steps.caption: one shared MLA latent per token, read by every head
steps.say: It sits on latent attention, so one selection per token serves every head, and the gather stays one list.
The indexer is new weights on a trained model. First, everything else is frozen.
It learns to match what dense attention would have looked at, summed over heads.
Then selection switches on, and the whole model trains to live with it.
The payoff is in decoding. Dense cost climbs with position. The sparse model stays nearly flat to the end.

scenes.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash at 1M tokens, GB
scenes.say: What it does not save is storage. Nothing is evicted, so the cache is even a little bigger. What drops is what each token reads.

scenes.label: of a sparse layer's prefill spent in the indexer at 10M tokens
scenes.say: And the scan still touches every token. At ten million tokens, the scorer is almost the whole layer.

scenes.text: Keep every token, read only the ones a cheap scorer ranks highest.
scenes.say: Keep every token, and read only the ones a cheap scorer ranks highest.

recap: An indexer scores, attention reads the top k
scenes.say: Score everything, read a little, and keep it all. Thanks for watching!
